reason: I’ll start building the skin model by joining surface cells into a layer.
expectation: I expect the junctions to connect the cells into a surface layer, though I’m unsure what else it will need.

alternatives.reason: The fibers and support cells also seem relevant to the skin, but I want to start with its surface.

effect: The surface cells now form a connected sheet, so I can add its protective outer layer.
reaction: The explanation makes clear why separate cells need junctions to form a boundary.
reason: Adding the tough outer layer seems like the next step toward a skin boundary that resists wear.
expectation: I expect it to strengthen the connected surface layer, though the skin model may still need support underneath.

alternatives.reason: The fibers and support cells likely form a supporting layer, but I want to finish the surface first.

effect: The surface barrier resists wear and unwanted passage, and I now understand that living cells replace its dead outer cells. I still need to build the supporting part of the skin.
reaction: The replacement of dead outer cells was a useful detail I hadn't expected.
reason: The fibers and support cells seem likely to make the supporting tissue needed for the layered skin model.
expectation: I expect them to form a supportive layer that can be combined with the surface barrier.

alternatives.reason: Connecting the supply network to the arm also seems useful, but the current goal is to build the skin model.

effect: The supporting layer is ready, and I understand that skin tissue includes material outside its cells as well as the cells themselves.
reaction: The role of collagen fibers in supporting the tissue is a useful detail.
reason: Joining the surface barrier to its supporting layer should complete the layered skin model.
expectation: I expect a layered skin model with a protective surface and support underneath.

alternatives.reason: The supply network will likely be useful for the arm, but the skin layers are ready to join now.

effect: The protective surface and supporting tissue now form layered skin; adding sensory endings seems like a useful next step.
reaction: Joining the layers clarified how their different jobs contribute to the skin.
reason: The sensory endings should add a way for the skin to detect contact or other sensations.
expectation: I expect the layered skin to gain sensory functions, though I’m unsure how it will connect to the arm.

alternatives.reason: Connecting the supply network to the arm also seems useful, but I want to finish equipping the skin first.

effect: The skin now detects contact as well as providing a boundary, and the goal has shifted to joining protection, supply and control.
reaction: Connecting skin sensation to nerve pathways makes its role in the reaching task clearer.
reason: This is the only offered combination, and it should connect the arm to its supply network.
expectation: I expect the arm to be linked to the circulation supplying oxygen and nutrients; the sensitive skin may need to be added afterward.

effect: The arm now has a supply route as well as nerve control, leaving the sensitive skin to be joined.
reaction: The distinction between supplying and directing the arm's work is clear.
reason: This is the only offered combination and should complete the connection between protection, supply and control.
expectation: I expect the sensitive skin to cover the supplied arm and connect its sensory role to the arm.

effect: The completed model connects the skin, arm, control and supply routes, while showing that the tissues still need ongoing energy and replacement.
reaction: Bringing the parts together was satisfying, and the reminder about ongoing upkeep gave the model a useful sense of being alive.

mostWorthwhile.text: Joining the surface barrier to the supporting layer was most worthwhile because it made the different jobs of the two skin layers clear.

leastWorthwhile.text: Connecting the supply network to the arm felt less engaging because it was the only offered combination and its purpose was already fairly clear.

surprise.text: I was surprised that the outermost skin cells are no longer living and are continually replaced by living cells deeper down.

arbitrary.text: No action felt particularly arbitrary; the combinations had clear purposes, though the final two were the only offered combinations.

continue.text: I would probably continue for another chapter to see how the model handles upkeep, though I would hope for more meaningful choices than the final forced combinations.
